gloss: chapters and verses; passages; phrases from a text

definitions.gloss: chapters and verses; passages from a text
definitions.explanation: Sections or passages of a written work, especially of classical texts, scriptures, or literary works. Often refers to the act of studying texts passage by passage.

examples.japanese: {聖書|せいしょ}の{章句|しょうく}を{引用|いんよう}する。
examples.english: To quote a passage from the Bible.

examples.japanese: {古典|こてん}の{章句|しょうく}を{暗記|あんき}するのは{大変|たいへん}だ。
examples.english: Memorizing passages from the classics is difficult.

examples.japanese: {論語|ろんご}の{有名|ゆうめい}な{章句|しょうく}は、{現代|げんだい}でも{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}に{親|した}しまれている。
examples.english: Famous passages from the Analects of Confucius are still enjoyed by many people today.

notes:
Composed of {章|しょう} (chapter) + {句|く} (phrase, verse). A somewhat literary term used when referring to passages from classical, religious, or important texts. In classical Chinese studies ({漢学|かんがく}), {章句|しょうく}の{学|がく} referred to the meticulous study of texts line by line.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {章句|しょうく}を{引|ひ}く: to cite a passage
- {章句|しょうく}を{暗唱|あんしょう}する: to recite passages from memory
- {有名|ゆうめい}な{章句|しょうく}: a famous passage

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {節|せつ}: section, verse -- a division of a text, less literary
- {一節|いっせつ}: a passage, a section -- refers to one specific part
- {文句|もんく}: phrase, words -- in modern usage usually means complaint, but originally meant a phrase of text
- {引用|いんよう}: quotation, citation -- the act of quoting rather than the passage itself
